evidence_context.text: OrbitVitals summary of the NASA web page "Wearable Tech for Space Station Research" (section "To sleep, perchance to dream"): The Wearable Monitoring investigation tested a light vest with built-in sensors that record heart rate and breathing during sleep without waking the wearer, to learn whether sleep quality is affected by changes in heart activity. Signal quality was reported as good, which supports its use for individual health monitoring on future flights.

OrbitVitals summary of the NASA web page "Science in Space: Week of Sept. 15, 2023 - Sleep on Station" (section "Science in Space: Week of Sept. 15, 2023 - Sleep on Station"): In the Sleep In Orbit investigation, each astronaut's natural sleep on Earth is recorded before and after the mission to form an individual baseline, and sleep recorded on the space station is then compared with that baseline.

OrbitVitals summary of the NASA web page "OCHMO-TB-031 Exercise Overview" (section "In-mission exercise monitoring"): Astronaut Strength, Conditioning, and Rehabilitation Specialists (ACERS) follow crew fitness during flight and tailor exercise prescriptions to each crew member's ability and performance. Ground teams review crew data, including physiological markers and the duration and intensity of exercise sessions, and strength prescriptions depend on the equipment on board.

citations.document_title: Wearable Tech for Space Station Research
citations.summary: The Wearable Monitoring investigation tested a light vest with built-in sensors that record heart rate and breathing during sleep without waking the wearer, to learn whether sleep quality is affected by changes in heart activity. Signal quality was reported as good, which supports its use for individual health monitoring on future flights.

citations.document_title: Science in Space: Week of Sept. 15, 2023 - Sleep on Station
citations.section: Science in Space: Week of Sept. 15, 2023 - Sleep on Station
citations.summary: In the Sleep In Orbit investigation, each astronaut's natural sleep on Earth is recorded before and after the mission to form an individual baseline, and sleep recorded on the space station is then compared with that baseline.

Astronaut Strength, Conditioning, and Rehabilitation Specialists (ACERS) follow crew fitness during flight and tailor exercise prescriptions to each crew member's ability and performance. Ground teams review crew data, including physiological markers and the duration and intensity of exercise sessions, and strength prescriptions depend on the equipment on board.
